mods.name: Urbex
mods.description: Procedural abandoned-city worldgen. A fork of Lost Cities by McJty.

releases.notes:
**Urbex** is procedural abandoned-city worldgen for Fabric — a hard fork of [Lost Cities](https://github.com/McJtyMods/LostCities) by McJty (MIT).

**Minecraft 26.2 · Fabric Loader 0.19.3+ · Fabric API 0.155.2+ · Java 25**

> **Beta.** 245 commits since the 0.1.0 alpha. The mod is in much better shape — cities have street hierarchy, everything it generates comes out of datapacks you can edit, and a fixed-seed digest check guards worldgen on every commit. It is still pre-1.0: **worlds made with 0.2.0 are not guaranteed to generate identically on a later version**, and 0.1.0 worlds will not continue as they were.

## Cities have streets now

0.1.0 decided street-or-park with a per-chunk coin flip, so a city was a blob of buildings with pavement scattered through it. 0.2.0 plans the road network first: **primary roads** on a coarse grid with their own density, **secondary roads** filling the blocks between them, **tertiary stubs** reaching into the remainder. Building lots are what is left over, not what won a toss.

Riding on that: primary roads **bridge water** on planned spans rather than stopping at the shoreline, and minor roads **slope** between city levels instead of stepping.

## Everything is a datapack

The old `UrbexProfile` / `Configuration` / TOML machinery is gone. Worldgen tuning is now a **preset** — a datapack registry entry with a real codec — and so is every building, part, palette, city style and decoration. Thirteen registries, all following one set of rules:

- **`extends` everywhere.** Any asset can build on another, field by field, root first. A file only has to state what it changes.
- **Every reference names its namespace.** `urbex:street_straight`, never `street_straight`. No asset reference has a code-side default, so a chain that never says which part a T-junction places refuses the world instead of quietly placing Urbex's.
- **Broken packs fail at load, naming the file.** Missing required wiring, an `extends` cycle, a mis-sized slice row, a palette marker that is not one character — all of it is a refusal while the world loads, not an exception from a worldgen worker halfway through a chunk.
- **[`docs/datapacks.md`](https://github.com/Arilas/urbex/blob/main/docs/datapacks.md)** is the authoring guide for all thirteen, and its JSON examples and quoted error messages are checked against the codecs by the test suite, so it cannot rot.

## Picking a preset

The world-creation screen has a **Cities** tab. **Disabled** is the default and leaves the world completely alone. Pick a preset, or **Customize this preset…** to edit a copy — the edited version is stored **in the world**, not in your config, so a save carries its own worldgen settings and re-creating a world keeps them.

Server owners: `dimensionsWithPresets` in `config/urbex/urbex.json`, as `minecraft:overworld=urbex:default` (or `…=urbex:default@urbex:standard` to also name a world style). Ids must name their namespace.

## Also in this release

- **`/urbex savepreset`** dumps the dimension's live, fully-resolved preset — after inheritance and after your customizations — as JSON you can ship as a datapack.
- **Worldgen is verified on every commit.** A headless fixed-seed server generates a chunk square and hashes what the block driver wrote; CI fails if it moves. It has caught real determinism regressions during this cycle, and it is what makes "this change does not move worldgen" a checked claim rather than a hope.
- **Decoration reaches the spawn area.** Assets used to load on the first server tick, after the spawn chunks had already generated undecorated.
- **Cross-chunk reads are gone**, and with them the errors they logged.
- **A mod icon**, so Mod Menu no longer shows a blank tile.

releases.notes:
First preview of **Urbex**, a Fabric-only hard fork of [Lost Cities](https://github.com/McJtyMods/LostCities) by McJty (MIT).

**Minecraft 26.2 · Fabric Loader 0.19.3+ · Fabric API · Forge Config API Port · Java 25**

> **Alpha.** It generates and it runs. This release exists to get it in front of people, not because it is finished. Worlds made with 0.1.0 are not guaranteed to generate identically on a later version.

## Why this fork exists

Lost Cities' worldgen was not reproducible from the world seed — in three separate ways:

- One `RandomSource` was shared across every chunk in a dimension and reseeded *after* city generation had already drawn from it, so ruins and part selection consumed the previous chunk's leftover state.
- Rubble and leaf placement ran off a `static int` no world seed ever touched.
- **City placement ignored the seed entirely.** Every world on a given profile put its cities in identical chunks at identical radii. Changing the seed did not move a single city.

All three are fixed. Randomness is now *addressed* — a stream is a pure function of the seed, a coordinate and a named purpose — so generation order cannot influence output.

## Also here

- **Parallel worldgen restored.** The per-dimension generation lock is gone, along with the shared mutable state that required it.
- **World height.** Six sites assumed a 0–255 world; they now read the level's real bounds.
- **Profiles are editable.** Previously the mod rewrote every profile JSON on launch and *then* read the directory, so your edits were overwritten before they were seen.
- **Startup.** An unknown `selectedProfile` fails at server start with the valid names listed, instead of an NPE during world init.

## Getting started

Cities generate in the `urbex:city` dimension by default. To get them in a normal overworld, use the **Cities** button on the world-creation screen. `/urbex` (or `/ubx`) has the commands.

## Not compatible with Lost Cities

Different mod id, namespace, saved-data ids and dimension. Lost Cities worlds, datapacks and configs will not load, and a Lost Cities seed will not reproduce here. That is deliberate.

## Known limitations

Tracked openly rather than hidden — #18 (a small residual order-dependence), #19, #20, #29 (an upstream highway-symmetry bug, not introduced here), and #21–#28, #30.

Full detail in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Arilas/urbex/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
